Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this — attached is the short questionnaire our security team uses for hosted vendors. The core asks for Zenara are:
1) Where does customer data live (region & physical controls)?
2) What are default retention periods for request payloads, logs, and backups?
3) How quickly can we request an immediate purge and what is the timeline to confirm?
4) Do you retain any customer content for model improvements or analytics by default?

Please send whatever level of detail you can, and any artifacts would be great (retention matrix, SOC2 pointers). We need this for our procurement review.

Hi Ava / Samuel —

Thanks — forwarding concise answers below to match your questionnaire. I put the operational/engineer-level details first, then a short summary for procurement. Let us know if you want a formal evidence pack.

OPERATIONAL RESPONSES
1) Data residency (hosted API):
   - Customers choose the primary region at account creation. For Zenara we can pin to US-West (Oregon) or US-East (N. Virginia) — data and persistent storage for that account are kept in the chosen AWS region.
   - Physical controls: we use cloud provider region boundaries + RBAC, VPC isolation for privileged components, and encryption at-rest (AES-256) for all persistent stores.

2) Default retention periods (hosted API):
   - Request payloads & model outputs: retained for 30 days by default. This retention applies to user-provided prompts and the generated text stored in the request store.
   - Structured logs & telemetry (ingestion/latency/error metrics): retained for 13 months in aggregated form; raw debug traces that contain request payloads follow the 30-day window and are deleted thereafter.
   - Backups & disaster-recovery snapshots: encrypted snapshots are retained for up to 90 days. Snapshots are stored in the customer region when possible; snapshot metadata includes a retention TTL.

3) Immediate purge process & timeline:
   - Customer-initiated purge: Zenara can trigger a manual erasure request via the Console (Data > Erase) or an API call.
   - Active stores: we remove items from the live request store within 24–72 hours of a verified request (depends on business-day validation and service tickets).
   - Cache and KV (prefix caches, inference caches): ephemeral caches are flushed within 24 hours by default; if Zenara requires accelerated eviction we run a targeted flush which completes within the same 24–72 hour window.
   - Snapshots & backups: snapshots are marked for expedited deletion and removed at the next snapshot GC cycle. In practice, full removal from off-site snapshot storage can take up to 30 days depending on provider retention windows; we provide an attestation once complete.

4) Use of customer content for model improvements:
   - By default, we do NOT use customer prompts/responses to train or improve base models. Any use of customer content for training is opt-in and contractually controlled.

PROCUREMENT-LEVEL SUMMARY (one paragraph)
Redwood stores account data in the customer-selected cloud region and retains request payloads/outputs for 30 days by default, aggregated telemetry for 13 months, and encrypted recovery snapshots for 90 days. Customers can request immediate erasure through the Console or API; live stores and caches are cleared within 24–72 hours, and backup/snapshot removal is completed within 30 days with confirmation. We do not use customer content for model training unless explicitly authorized.

ARTIFACTS
Attached is a retention matrix that maps store type -> default TTL -> purge timeline. We can also provide SOC2 evidence excerpts and the deletion attestation after a test purge.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if your team wants to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Ava / team — quick follow-up on a couple of technical details you might surface to your InfoSec folks:

- Backups: the 90-day snapshot retention is an operational maximum. For accounts subject to strict data residency we can configure shorter snapshot TTLs (e.g., 14 or 30 days) as part of the onboarding contract. Shorter TTLs will be enforced at the snapshot lifecycle manager and included in the attestation we provide.

- Immutable provider retention: some low-level provider caches (object-storage replication windows, provider-side replication logs) may have short replication/GC windows outside Redwood control. We track those windows and include them in the deletion attestation; typically these are measured in hours to a few days, not months.

- Evidence pack: attached is a short SOC2 checklist excerpt and the high-level deletion playbook we'll use for a formal erasure test. If Zenara wants a formal test run, we recommend scheduling a test on a non-production tenant so we can provide the full attestation PDF.

Jonas Weber
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
